scenario: [LCCO.3.7] item 2: "When a synthesized terminal fires -- an `after` follow-up or a continuation sibling ([RLOW.14.7]) -- before any of its actions runs: one value for each `call` in its own body that has no `as` or a computed `as`, in source order. A `call` with a continuation in that body takes none: it carries a literal `as`, or the compiler refuses it ([LCCO.3.8])." Rule `r` calls `svc.first` with no `as`, which takes `g0` when `r` fires. Its `after 5_s:` body reads no binding of `r`, so the clause takes no value ([LCCO.3.7] item 1). When the follow-up fires it calls `svc.plain` with no `as` (call 0, `g1`), `svc.probe` with a continuation and `as "probe"` (call 1, no value, issued as `probe`), and `svc.plain` again (call 2, `g2`). PATH PINNED: `lcrs_3_1_generated_calls` in dsc.rete, which mints one `fn_gensym` bind in the follow-up's frame for each plain call and none for the continued one, evaluated in source order by each runtime when the follow-up fires. A continued call that took a value would make the last call `g3`. The plain calls' correlations are named from the follow-up, `$r_after_0`, so each is `$$r_after_0_c<N>_g<k>` ([LCCO.3.4], [LLEX.10.6.1]).
rules_ds:
schema Reply scope ttl 1_h:
    corr: String
    code: Int

service svc.first:
    kwarg n: Int
    no response

service svc.plain:
    kwarg n: Int
    no response

service svc.probe:
    kwarg n: Int
    response Reply

schema Job scope explicit:
    id: Int

rule r:
    Job j
->
    call svc.first n: j.id nocooldown
    after 5_s:
        call svc.plain n: 2 nocooldown
        call svc.probe n: 3 nocooldown as "probe"
            on response.code == 200:
                log info "ok"
        call svc.plain n: 4 nocooldown
